note: Year 11 Foundation Foundation Spring Block 5 Constructions and loci: one set of templates per small step of the White Rose Maths scheme of learning.

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S1 Use geometrical equipment
templates.text: A line measures [[a]] cm and [[b]] mm on a ruler. Write the length in millimetres.

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S1 Use geometrical equipment
templates.text: You read [[x]]° on the inner scale of a protractor. What is the angle on the outer scale?

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S1 Use geometrical equipment
templates.text: To draw a circle of diameter [[d]] cm, what radius do you set on compasses?

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S1 Use geometrical equipment
templates.text: A triangle's sides are measured as [[a]] cm, [[b]] cm and [[c]] cm to the nearest mm. Explain why drawing it needs compasses and say which two radii to use after drawing the [[a]] cm side. (2 marks)
templates.answer: Arcs of radius [[b]] cm and [[c]] cm from the two ends of the [[a]] cm side meet at the third vertex

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S2 Accurately draw triangles
templates.text: Can a triangle have sides [[a]] cm, [[b]] cm and [[c]] cm?
templates.answer: [[a + b > c && a + c > b && b + c > a|if:Yes/No]]

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S2 Accurately draw triangles
templates.text: Two sides of a triangle are [[a]] cm and [[b]] cm. Between what values must the third side lie?
templates.answer: More than [[abs(a - b)]] cm and less than [[a + b]] cm

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S2 Accurately draw triangles
templates.text: To draw a triangle with sides [[a]] cm, [[b]] cm and [[c]] cm you draw the [[a]] cm side then use compasses. What two compass radii do you use?
templates.answer: [[b]] cm from one end and [[c]] cm from the other end, so the arcs cross at the third vertex

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S2 Accurately draw triangles
templates.text: A triangle has sides [[a]] cm, [[b]] cm and $x$ cm where $x$ is a whole number. List the possible values of $x$. (3 marks)
templates.answer: $[[abs(a - b) + 1]]$ to $[[a + b - 1]]$ (that is [[a + b - 1 - abs(a - b)]] values)

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S3 Accurately draw polygons (E)
templates.text: To construct a regular polygon with [[n]] sides inside a circle, what angle at the centre does each side make?

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S3 Accurately draw polygons (E)
templates.text: A regular [[n]]-sided polygon is drawn. What is the size of each interior angle?

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S3 Accurately draw polygons (E)
templates.text: To draw a regular hexagon of side [[s]] cm using compasses, what radius do you set and why?
templates.answer: [[s]] cm: the radius equals the side length because the triangles at the centre are equilateral

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S3 Accurately draw polygons (E)
templates.text: A regular octagon is constructed inside a circle of radius [[r]] cm. (a) What angle at the centre does each side make? (b) What is the interior angle? (c) Is the side length equal to [[r]] cm? Explain. (3 marks)
templates.answer: (a) 45°  (b) 135°  (c) No: the triangle at the centre has a 45° angle, so it is not equilateral: the side is about [[0.765 * r|dp:1]] cm, shorter than the radius

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S4 Construct a perpendicular bisector
templates.text: $AB$ is [[l]] cm long. When you construct its perpendicular bisector, how far is the midpoint from $A$?

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S4 Construct a perpendicular bisector
templates.text: $P$ is on the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ and $PA$ = [[p]] cm. How long is $PB$? Why?
templates.answer: [[p]] cm: every point on the perpendicular bisector is the same distance from $A$ and $B$

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S4 Construct a perpendicular bisector
templates.text: When constructing the perpendicular bisector of a line [[l]] cm long, Mia sets her compasses to [[r]] cm. Will it work? Explain.
templates.answer: [[r * 2 > l|if:Yes/No]]: the radius must be more than half the line, [[l / 2]] cm, for the arcs to cross

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S4 Construct a perpendicular bisector
templates.text: $AB$ is [[6 * k]] cm. $P$ is on the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ with $PA$ = [[5 * k]] cm. How far is $P$ from the line $AB$? (3 marks)
templates.answer: [[4 * k]] cm (by Pythagoras: [[5 * k]]² − [[3 * k]]² = [[4 * k]]²)

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S5 Construct an angle bisector
templates.text: An angle of [[a]]° is bisected. How big is each half?

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S5 Construct an angle bisector
templates.text: The bisector of angle $ABC$ makes an angle of [[a]]° with $BA$. How big is angle $ABC$?

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S5 Construct an angle bisector
templates.text: You construct a 60° angle and bisect it [[n]] times. What angle do you get?

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S5 Construct an angle bisector
templates.text: Describe how to construct an angle of [[k]]° using only compasses and a straight edge, starting from a 60° angle. (3 marks)
templates.answer: [[k == 30|if:Bisect the 60° angle/]][[k == 45|if:Construct a 90° angle then bisect it/]][[k == 15|if:Bisect the 60° angle to make 30° then bisect again/]][[k == 120|if:Construct two 60° angles next to each other/]]

templates.subtopic: Construct a perpendicular from or to a point
templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S6 Construct a perpendicular from or to a point
templates.text: Point $P$ is [[h]] cm from a line $L$ measured along the perpendicular. What is the shortest distance from $P$ to $L$?
templates.answer: [[h]] cm: the perpendicular distance is the shortest

templates.subtopic: Construct a perpendicular from or to a point
templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S6 Construct a perpendicular from or to a point
templates.text: A triangle has a base of [[b]] cm and a perpendicular height of [[h]] cm. Work out its area.
templates.answer: [[b * h / 2]] cm²

templates.subtopic: Construct a perpendicular from or to a point
templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S6 Construct a perpendicular from or to a point
templates.text: $P$ is [[4 * k]] cm from a line, measured along the perpendicular. $Q$ is on the line [[3 * k]] cm along from the foot of that perpendicular. Work out $PQ$.

templates.subtopic: Construct a perpendicular from or to a point
templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S6 Construct a perpendicular from or to a point
templates.text: A triangle has a base of [[b]] cm and area [[A]] cm². (a) Work out its perpendicular height. (b) A point is constructed [[h]] cm above the base on a perpendicular through its midpoint. Is the area bigger or smaller than $A$? Explain. (3 marks)
templates.answer: (a) [[2 * A / b]] cm  (b) [[h > 2 * A / b|if:bigger/smaller]]: area = ½ × [[b]] × [[h]] = [[b * h / 2]] cm²

templates.subtopic: Locus of distance from a point or a straight line
templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S7 Locus of distance from a point or a straight line
templates.text: Describe the locus of points that are [[r]] cm from a fixed point $A$.
templates.answer: A circle with centre $A$ and radius [[r]] cm

templates.subtopic: Locus of distance from a point or a straight line
templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S7 Locus of distance from a point or a straight line
templates.text: Points are exactly [[r]] cm from a line segment $AB$ of length [[l]] cm. Describe the shape and work out its perimeter in terms of $\pi$.
templates.answer: Two straight lines [[l]] cm long and two semicircular ends: perimeter [[2 * l]] + [[2 * r]]$\pi$ cm

templates.subtopic: Locus of distance from a point or a straight line
templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S7 Locus of distance from a point or a straight line
templates.text: A dog is tied by a [[r]] m rope to a post. Describe the region it can reach and work out its area in terms of $\pi$.
templates.answer: A circle of radius [[r]] m; area $[[r * r]]\pi$ m²

templates.subtopic: Locus of distance from a point or a straight line
templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S7 Locus of distance from a point or a straight line
templates.text: The region within [[r]] cm of a line segment $AB$ of length [[l]] cm is shaded. Work out its area in terms of $\pi$. (3 marks)

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S8 Locus equidistant from two points
templates.text: Describe the locus of points equidistant from two points $A$ and $B$ that are [[d]] cm apart.
templates.answer: The perpendicular bisector of $AB$, passing through the midpoint [[d / 2]] cm from each

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S8 Locus equidistant from two points
templates.text: $A$ is (0, 0) and $B$ is ([[2 * a]], 0). Write the equation of the locus of points equidistant from $A$ and $B$.

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S8 Locus equidistant from two points
templates.text: $A$ is (0, [[a]]) and $B$ is (0, [[b]]). The locus of points equidistant from $A$ and $B$ is a line. Write its equation.

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S8 Locus equidistant from two points
templates.text: A mast must be equidistant from two towns $A$ and $B$ that are [[d]] km apart and within [[r]] km of $A$. Describe the possible positions and the nearest distance from $A$. (3 marks)
templates.answer: On the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ and inside the circle of radius [[r]] km about $A$; the nearest point is the midpoint, [[d / 2]] km from $A$

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S9 Locus equidistant from two lines
templates.text: Describe the locus of points equidistant from two lines that meet at an angle of [[x]]°.
templates.answer: The bisector of the angle: a line making [[x / 2]]° with each line

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S9 Locus equidistant from two lines
templates.text: Two parallel lines are [[d]] cm apart. Describe the locus of points equidistant from both.
templates.answer: A parallel line midway between them, [[d / 2]] cm from each

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S9 Locus equidistant from two lines
templates.text: Lines $AB$ and $AC$ meet at $A$ with angle $BAC$ = [[x]]°. A point $P$ on the bisector is [[d]] cm from $A$. Find its distance from $AB$ to 1 decimal place.
templates.answer: [[d * sin(x / 2)|dp:1]] cm

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S9 Locus equidistant from two lines
templates.text: A path runs between two straight fences that meet at [[x]]°. A walker keeps equally far from both fences. Describe the path and the angle it makes with each fence. (2 marks)
templates.answer: The angle bisector; [[x / 2]]° with each fence

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S10 Solve problems with loci
templates.text: A treasure is within [[r]] m of a tree. Describe the region.
templates.answer: Inside (and on) a circle of radius [[r]] m centred on the tree

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S10 Solve problems with loci
templates.text: A point must be within [[r]] m of a post $P$ and closer to $A$ than $B$. Describe the region.
templates.answer: Inside the circle of radius [[r]] m about $P$ and on $A$'s side of the perpendicular bisector of $AB$

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S10 Solve problems with loci
templates.text: A goat is tied to the corner of a [[w]] m by [[l]] m shed with a [[r]] m rope. What fraction of a full circle can the goat reach outside the shed, and what is the area in terms of $\pi$?
templates.answer: Three quarters of a circle: area $\frac{3}{4} \times [[r * r]]\pi$ = $[[3 * r * r / 4|dp:2]]\pi$ m²

templates.source: Y11 Foundation Spring B5 Constructions and loci · S10 Solve problems with loci
templates.text: A radio mast covers points within [[r]] km. Two towns are [[d]] km apart . Describe the region covered by both masts (one at each town). (3 marks)
templates.answer: The overlapping lens between the two circles of radius [[r]] km; its width along the line joining them is [[2 * r - d]] km
